description: This article sets out reference datasets of the primary exhaust of rocket engines, modelled up to the nozzle exit, for use in global launch emission inventories when detailed engine models are not available. Steffen Callsen, Moritz Herberhold, Jascha Wilken and Martin Sippel of the German Aerospace Center published it in CEAS Space Journal in September 2026. The data cover nine generic engines at a common 2,200 kN thrust class, liquid oxygen with kerosene, methane or hydrogen, and nitrogen tetroxide with UDMH, each in staged combustion and gas generator cycles, plus a solid rocket motor, and an exploratory treatment of fuel film cooling; engine cycle and film cooling prove critical for black carbon fractions, and the results are compared with existing inventories. Coverage is generic engine classes used by current launchers worldwide. Format and access: tables in an open access PDF; the article states that no separate dataset files were generated. Licence: CC-BY-4.0; free. Caveats: values come from 0D equilibrium modelling of generic engines, not measurements of specific engines. It supports environmental impact estimates of launch activity for climate studies. A related catalogue record is DLR's IGEL 2024 launch emission inventory, which uses such exhaust indices.
